newsitem.title: FRANCE: Frenchmen released by India return home.
newsitem.headline: Frenchmen released by India return home.

text.p: Three Frenchmen and a Malagasy national released by India after 15 months in custody on suspicion of spying returned to Paris on Saturday, the French Foreign Ministry said.
The fate of two other French crewmembers of the catamaran "Galathee" will be decided by a court in Kerala on April 2.

Frenchmen Thierry Proust, Herve Blanchet, Pierre-Hugues Lejeune and Vincent Matthew of Madagascar were greeted on their arrival by officials and by former deputy foreign minister Jean-Francois Deniau who pleaded their case earlier in India.
India released the four earlier this week but two Frenchmen remain behind.

Archeologist Francois Clavel and the catamaran's captain Philippe Elle were indicted for spying for allegedly carrying out illegal underwater surveys that could aid an enemy in anti-submarine warfare.
An Indian businessman and a former Indian politician were also charged.
The crew members were arrested in December 1995 by harbour police for allegedly carrying out an unauthorised survey of the seabed near the southern port of Cochin, site of a major Indian naval base.
Elle has told Reuters that the survey was meant to determine if the harbour was suitable for aquaculture and could serve as a base for pleasure sailing.
The "Galathee" crew was also interested in studying a 16th-century ship wreck, he said.
